title: Fynaptix · Defense Tech Research
heading: Defense Technology Intelligence
subheading: AI battlefield software, drones, autonomy & European rearmament
disclaimer: Not financial advice. This page organizes public information for research purposes only — not a recommendation to buy or sell any security. Defense names carry policy, program-concentration, and valuation risk. Verify current prices and do your own due diligence before investing.

kpis.label: Europe's 2025 defence spend rose 14% to $864B; Germany's climbed 24% YoY to $114B, pushing it above NATO's 2%-of-GDP guideline (2.3%) for the first time since 1990, while Spain's jumped 50% to $40.2B; the Hague 2025 NATO summit's 5%-of-GDP-by-2035 target (3.5% core plus 1.5% broader security) and the EU's €800B 'ReArm Europe' framework keep the multi-year runway intact even as individual names wobble week to week

kpis.sub: 2026 YTD · DEFENSE TECH VC, ALREADY WELL PAST 2025's $9.6B FULL-YEAR RECORD
kpis.label: Castelion's $1B Series C (Aug 20, JPMorgan/a16z/Carlyle, $13B valuation) for hypersonic-missile production and Saronic's fresh $55M add-on (early Sep) keep capital flowing even as Anduril's own targeted $100B round, first reported Jul 24, remains unclosed nearly eight weeks later as of Sep 14 — CEO Brian Schimpf has said he's "not sure the market is particularly rational on the pricing right now" and won't rush an IPO "in the middle of a hype cycle"

Defense Autonomous Warfare Group request inside a record $75B FY27 drone/counter-drone budget ask ($13.4B total autonomy request); the Sep 3 stopgap (House passed 370-48) funds government through Dec 11 at FY26 levels but leaves FY27 appropriations, the CCA Increment 2 downselect (Air Force now running concept work with as many as 20 vendors, ~10 months from a decision), and Golden Dome's reconciliation-dependent funding unresolved — DAWG's own head has said he isn't sure his team gets funded in FY27

kpis.sub: AVAV Q1 FY27 REVENUE · RECORD BEAT, SEP 9
kpis.label: Record funded backlog hit $1.5B (+37% YoY, +23% sequentially) on a 1.4x book-to-bill ratio; adjusted EPS of $0.59 blew past the ~$0.25-0.30 consensus and shares jumped as much as 10% to the high-$140s, the stock's best stretch since the SCAR/BADGER restatement — though the securities-fraud class actions tied to that episode are still working through the courts

tiers.label: Established / Software & Primes
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: Shares near $167 (Sep 12, ~$402B market cap) after a volatile stretch that included a 43% rally over the trailing month; DA Davidson lifted its target to $250 on an 'AI sovereignty' thesis (Sep 11) and Rosenblatt reiterated Buy at $225 after AIPCon 11, even with the stock trading near 143x trailing earnings
rows.watch for: Michael Burry's Sep 2 case that the market cap (then ~$432B) could eventually fall below $100B hasn't been retracted — the deferred-revenue and stock-based-comp dynamics he flagged are unchanged, and a name that can rally 43% in a month on sentiment can give it back just as fast

rows.angle: A new $7.3M US Marine Corps unmanned-ground-vehicle order and Deutsche Bank's Sep 1 Buy reiteration weren't enough to stop the drift — shares fell to ~€988 (Sep 14), down roughly 36% YTD and underperforming the DAX, still digesting the F126 guidance cut
rows.watch for: JPMorgan placed Rheinmetall on a Negative Catalyst Watch Sep 10 even while 18 of 18 covering analysts keep Buy/Strong-Buy ratings intact — a sign sentiment may be turning before the fundamentals do

rows.angle: New CEO Sam Mehta laid out a reorganized three-pillar portfolio (multi-domain sensing, spectrum dominance, missiles) at the Sep 9 Jefferies conference and reaffirmed guidance; shares have traded in a wide $265-295 band since
rows.watch for: Chris Kubasik's Aug 17 ouster was for conduct 'inconsistent with company values,' not performance, but nearly a month on the company still hasn't detailed what happened, and Golden Dome's own FY27 funding remains at risk per Gen. Guetlein's Aug 12 warning

rows.angle: Shares eased to 1,839p (Sep 14, £55.59B market cap) off the 2,360p 52-week high, still backed by a record £84.0B H1 order backlog and July's raised full-year guidance (8-10% sales growth, 11-13% EPS growth)
rows.watch for: The pullback from the 52-week high is the first real test of whether the market believes the raised guidance, with H2 execution still to prove out

tiers.label: High-Growth Autonomy Pure-Plays
tiers.note: Tiered by maturity/risk — not a ranked buy list.

rows.angle: The Sep 9 Q1 FY27 print was a resounding beat — $480.5M revenue (+5.7% YoY, beating estimates by ~5%), $0.59 adjusted EPS against a ~$0.25-0.30 consensus, and a record $1.5B funded backlog (+37% YoY) on a 1.4x book-to-bill ratio — shares jumped as much as 10% to the high-$140s
rows.watch for: The securities-fraud class actions tied to the SCAR/BADGER restatement are still working through the courts; a strong quarter doesn't retroactively resolve the disclosure issue that triggered them

rows.angle: Shares firmed into the mid-to-high $40s as Canaccord ($135), BTIG ($104) and Clear Street ($86) all raised targets following a Q2 beat-and-raise, with consensus now $105.62 across 21 analysts (Strong Buy); GE Aerospace's durability testing on the GEK800 engine keeps the CCA-engine optionality alive toward a targeted $150M of 2027 turbojet revenue
rows.watch for: Backlog of $2.08B is real, but Kratos remains outside the June CCA Increment 1 production award (Anduril & General Atomics) and is one of as many as 20 companies the Air Force is now engaging for Increment 2, a process roughly 10 months from a decision

rows.angle: Shares held near $8.12 (Sep 11) as the Blue Ops/Havoc maritime-autonomy tie-up and the now-closed Apium Swarm Robotics acquisition build out the platform story; the stock carries a $16 consensus target after a recent Sell-to-Hold upgrade, against management's $150-180M revenue target
rows.watch for: Recent insider share sales are a caution flag on conviction even as the maritime and swarm-autonomy pushes look like a genuine platform shift; whether they convert into contracted revenue is the open question

rows.angle: Q2 revenue jumped 67% sequentially and more than 13x YoY to $83.8M on Counter-UAS demand, but the company printed a $0.19/share loss versus $0.13 expected and shares fell nearly 4% on the Sep 9 print as rising costs and cash burn overshadowed the top-line growth
rows.watch for: A Form 144 insider-sale filing adds to the overhang; the stock needs to show the cost structure can scale with revenue rather than chase it

private_watchlist.name: Anduril
private_watchlist.note: Talks first reported Jul 24 remain unclosed nearly eight weeks later, as of Sep 14 — more than 3x the $30.5B mark from just over a year ago and up from the $61B May 2026 round (Thrive Capital, a16z). CEO Brian Schimpf continues to say the company isn't in a rush to IPO 'in the middle of a hype cycle' even while pursuing this raise; TITAN production orders and June's FQ-44A CCA award keep revenue scaling in the meantime.

private_watchlist.name: Shield AI
private_watchlist.note: No new financing this period; still marked by the ~$1.5-2B round (Mar 2026) that valued the company at $12.7B, co-led by Advent International and JPMorgan's Security & Resiliency Initiative, which also funded the Aechelon Technology simulation-firm acquisition. Continuing to compete for the Navy's up-to-$800M ISR task-order pool using the V-BAT drone, with Poland's Ministry of National Defence having awarded Shield AI a V-BAT contract as the first NATO eastern-flank nation to deploy the platform.

private_watchlist.name: Saronic
private_watchlist.note: A fresh $55M add-on round in early September keeps capital flowing on top of the $1.75B Series D (Kleiner Perkins) that set the $9.25B mark. The company established an autonomous-ship test site at the Port of Gulfport in August to commission its 180-foot Marauder Medium Unmanned Surface Vessels, continuing to build toward a stated target of 20+ autonomous surface vessels a year by 2027 out of its Franklin, Louisiana shipyard.

private_watchlist.name: Helsing
private_watchlist.note: No new financing this period; still marked by the $1.8B Series E closed Jul 13, 2026 (Lightspeed, General Catalyst, JPMorgan, Iconiq) — the largest defence-tech round in European history. Continues fielding the HX-2 strike drone in Ukraine and building out its Altra battle-management software and CA-1 Europa uncrewed-fighter concept.

bear_case.title: Public-market valuations still elevated, in both directions
bear_case.description: Palantir trades near 143x trailing earnings even after pulling back from its early-September highs, with Burry's unretracted case that the market cap could eventually fall below $100B still hanging over the stock; the S&P Aerospace & Defense sub-index trades around 32x forward earnings versus roughly 20x for the broader S&P 500. Rheinmetall shows the same dynamic can cut the other way — down ~36% YTD despite a record order book — proof that sentiment, not just fundamentals, is setting these prices.

bear_case.title: AeroVironment's legal overhang survives even a blowout quarter
bear_case.description: The Sep 9 beat — record $480.5M revenue, $0.59 EPS, a $1.5B backlog — sent shares up 10%, but the securities-fraud class actions tied to January's SCAR/BADGER stop-work order and the resulting $87.3M restatement error are still proceeding through the courts; a strong print doesn't retroactively fix the disclosure issue that triggered the litigation.

bear_case.title: The defense-tech VC boom still looks like a bubble
bear_case.description: Anduril's targeted $100B round remains unclosed nearly eight weeks after first being reported, and CEO Brian Schimpf has said outright he isn't sure the market is pricing the sector rationally — even as Castelion closed a $1B round at a $13B valuation on Aug 20 and Saronic added another $55M in early September, showing capital is still chasing the space at a pace some insiders themselves call unsustainable.

bear_case.title: December's funding cliff is still just a cliff, not a resolution
bear_case.description: The Sep 3 stopgap funds government (and defense) through Dec 11 at FY26 levels, but Congress has passed only 3 of 12 full-year spending bills in the House and none in the Senate; the $54.6B DAWG autonomy line item, the CCA Increment 2 downselect, and Golden Dome's reconciliation-dependent funding all remain unresolved with the clock reset rather than stopped.

bear_case.title: Governance and program-execution risk hits even established primes
bear_case.description: L3Harris's Aug 17 ouster of CEO Chris Kubasik for conduct 'inconsistent with company values' still hasn't been fully explained a month later, and JPMorgan's Sep 10 Negative Catalyst Watch on Rheinmetall landed even as the company posted a record order book — a reminder that backlogs don't insulate a prime from sudden leadership or sentiment shocks.

catalysts.title: DA Davidson lifts Palantir target to $250 on "AI sovereignty" thesis
catalysts.description: Follows Rosenblatt's Buy reiteration at $225 after AIPCon 11; shares near $167 after a 43% one-month rally, still shadowed by Burry's unretracted valuation critique.

catalysts.title: JPMorgan puts Rheinmetall on Negative Catalyst Watch
catalysts.description: Flag lands even as all 18 covering analysts keep Buy/Strong-Buy ratings; shares extend their YTD slide to roughly 36%, still absorbing the F126 guidance cut.

catalysts.title: AeroVironment posts blowout Q1 FY27 results, shares jump ~10%
catalysts.description: $480.5M revenue and $0.59 adjusted EPS beat consensus; funded backlog hits a record $1.5B (+37% YoY) on a 1.4x book-to-bill ratio.

catalysts.title: New L3Harris CEO Sam Mehta unveils reorganized three-pillar portfolio
catalysts.description: Multi-domain sensing, spectrum dominance and missiles, presented at the Jefferies Global Industrials Conference nearly a month after Kubasik's conduct-related ouster; guidance reaffirmed.

catalysts.title: Ondas misses on EPS despite 67% sequential revenue growth
catalysts.description: Counter-UAS demand drove Q2 revenue to $83.8M, but a wider-than-expected loss and a Form 144 insider-sale filing sent shares down nearly 4%.

catalysts.title: House passes stopgap funding bill 370-48, averting a shutdown
catalysts.description: Funds government including defense through Dec 11 at FY26 levels, leaving FY27 appropriations and the CCA Increment 2 downselect unresolved into December.

etfs.name: Global X Defense Tech
etfs.summary: Tilted toward Palantir and autonomy pure-plays, with almost 38% annualized returns since its Sept 2023 inception; this week's PLTR volatility and AVAV's post-earnings pop make for a choppier short-term read than the cap-weighted primes indices, even as the long-run trend holds

etfs.name: iShares US Aerospace & Defense
etfs.summary: Largest in category at ~$13.3B AUM and 0.38% expense ratio; broad US primes exposure has stayed largely insulated from this week's small-cap drone, PLTR and AVAV swings

etfs.name: Invesco Aerospace & Defense
etfs.summary: 0.58% expense ratio; broader diversification across commercial aerospace names (Boeing, GE Aerospace, RTX) tempers pure-play defense-tech volatility relative to ITA

etfs.name: Select STOXX Europe Defense
etfs.summary: ~$1.1B AUM across just 23 holdings, 0.5% expense ratio; European names continue absorbing Rheinmetall's negative-catalyst-watch-driven share drift even as Germany's 24% YoY defence-spend increase (to $114B) and Spain's 50% jump (to $40.2B) keep the backlog outlook growing

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: BAE Systems
positions.note: Record £84.0B H1 order backlog and July's raised full-year guidance (8-10% sales growth, 11-13% EPS growth, >£2B free cash flow) are unchallenged by any negative news this period, even as shares eased to 1,839p off the 2,360p 52-week high — still the most straightforward core holding, UK-listed with no wrapper needed; weight trimmed slightly to fund a new AVAV speculative position.

positions.name: Kratos Defense
positions.note: Three sell-side targets (Canaccord to $135, BTIG to $104, Clear Street to $86) all moved up post-Q2 beat-and-raise, consensus now $105.62 across 21 analysts, and GE Aerospace's GEK800 engine testing keeps the CCA-engine option alive toward a targeted $150M of 2027 turbojet revenue — still speculative given exclusion from the June CCA Increment 1 award and lingering dilution from August's $1.4B follow-on. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Red Cat Holdings
positions.note: The Blue Ops/Havoc maritime-autonomy tie-up and the now-closed Apium Swarm Robotics acquisition keep building the platform story, and the stock carries a $16 consensus target after a Sell-to-Hold upgrade, but recent insider share sales are enough of a conviction flag to trim this week — stays speculative, small size only. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: AeroVironment
positions.note: The Sep 9 Q1 FY27 beat was resounding — $480.5M revenue (+5.7% YoY), $0.59 adjusted EPS against a ~$0.25-0.30 consensus, and a record $1.5B funded backlog (+37% YoY, 1.4x book-to-bill) — shares jumped ~10%, enough to justify a small speculative position even though the SCAR/BADGER securities-fraud class actions are still working through the courts and represent a real chance of zero. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: L3Harris
positions.note: New CEO Sam Mehta reorganized the portfolio into three pillars and reaffirmed guidance at the Sep 9 Jefferies conference, but Kubasik's Aug 17 ouster for conduct 'inconsistent with company values' still hasn't been detailed nearly a month later, and Golden Dome's reconciliation-dependent FY27 funding remains at risk per Gen. Guetlein's Aug 12 warning. Also sits in the Space sleeve via satellite work — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Rheinmetall
positions.note: A record H1 book-to-bill above 3x hasn't stopped shares sliding to ~€988 (down ~36% YTD), and JPMorgan's Sep 10 Negative Catalyst Watch — even alongside 18-of-18 analyst Buy ratings — suggests sentiment may be turning before the fundamentals do; stays a watch until the price reflects the order book. Directly accessible from the UK without a US wrapper.

positions.name: Palantir
positions.note: DA Davidson's Sep 11 target hike to $250 and a 43% one-month rally to ~$167 (market cap ~$402B) show the AI-sovereignty narrative is still working, but Burry's unretracted case that the cap could eventually fall below $100B, plus a ~143x trailing P/E, keep this too rich to hold here. Also anchors the AI sleeve — don't double-count. Needs a US wrapper.

positions.name: Ondas Holdings
positions.note: Q2 revenue jumped 67% sequentially to $83.8M on Counter-UAS demand, but the company missed on EPS (-$0.19 vs -$0.13 expected), shares fell nearly 4% on the print, and a Form 144 filing signals an insider intends to sell — moving this to Avoid until the cost structure shows it can scale with revenue rather than outrun it.
